data.name: Nagarajan
data.long_meaning: Nagarajan is a name derived from the Sanskrit language, meaning 'King of Serpents'. This powerful and majestic name is believed to bring protection, courage, and wisdom. It is also associated with the Hindu deity Nagaraja, who is the king of all serpents and the lord of the underworld.

historical_references.reference: Nagarajan was a prominent Chola warrior and commander during the reign of Rajaraja Chola I (985-1014 CE). He is believed to have played a significant role in the expansion of the Chola empire, particularly in the southern and eastern regions.

Nagarajan is also mentioned in the 13th century Tamil epic 'Silapathikaram' as a wealthy and influential person in the city of Madurai during the Sangam period (approximately 200 BCE to 300 CE). He is known for his generosity and his patronage of art and literature.

Derived from the Sanskrit language, Nagarajan is composed of two parts: ‘Nagara,’ which means ‘city,’ and ‘Rajan,’ which means ‘king.’ This name is believed to represent the king of the city or the ruler of the town. In Hindu mythology, Nagarajan is also identified with the deity Nāga, who is the king of all serpents and holds great spiritual power. This name has a rich cultural and religious history, making it a popular choice for parents seeking to honor their heritage and traditions.
